3. His grievance is that the respondents though having concluded the proceedings have failed to comply the Act of 2013 and have passed the final award under the provisions of J&K Land Acquisition Act, 1990 Svt.
4.

The question now arises is whether the acquisition proceedings which had been initiated prior to the commencement of 2013 Act would continue under the previous act and the award would also be passed under the Act of 1990.

5. Respondents have submitted that the petitioners cannot be paid compensation under 2013 Act, as has been held and in support of this they have relied upon judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in "Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd. (BPCL) and others Vs. Nisar Ahmed Ganai and others", 2022 AIR (SC) 5026 and relying upon the said judgment, they have submitted that the relief claimed by the petitioner in this petition cannot be granted.

Petitioners in their rejoinder while referring to the provisions as contained in Section 95, 96 and 97 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 and Clause 2(5) of Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2019, contend that these provisions were not prompt to the notice of Hon'ble Supreme Court.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that had these provisions brought to the knowledge of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the order/judgment which have been issued could not have been passed in that manner.

7. Para No. 19 of the rejoinder filed by the petitioner is reproduced as under: -
19.

That in view of the fact that section 95, 96, 97 and 103 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, clause 2(5), 2(13) and 2(14) of Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2019 and clause 3, 4 and clause 6 of Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Adaption of Central Laws), Order 2020, were not brought to the notice of the Hon'ble Supreme Court while rendering the judgement titled "Bharat petroleum Corp Ltd, (BPCL) and others vs. Nisar Ahmad Ganai and others" (Civil Appeal number 6781-6783 of 2022), as such, the judgement cannot be treated as a precedent on this issue and should be treated as given per incuriam and must be held to have passed sub-silentio.

sentences.text: "40 'Incuria 'literally means 'carelessness'.
In practice per incuriam appears to mean per ignoratium.
English courts have developed this principle in relaxation of the rule of stare decisis.
The 'quotable in law 'is avoided and ignored if it is rendered, 'in ignoratium of a statute or other binding authority'.

(Young v. Bristol Aeroplane Co.
Ltd. )

sentences.text: Same has been accepted, approved and adopted by this Court while interpreting Article 141 of the Constitution which embodies the doctrine of precedents as a matter of law.

In Jaisri Sahu v. Rajdewan Dubey this Court while pointing out the procedure to be followed when conflicting decisions are placed before a bench extracted a passage from Halsbury's Laws of England incorporating one of the exceptions when the decision of an appellate court is not binding.
41. Does this principle extend and apply to a conclusion of law, which was neither raised nor preceded by any consideration.
In other words can such conclusions be considered as declaration of law?
Here again the English courts and jurists have carved out an exception to the rule of precedents.
It has been explained as rule of sub-silentio.

"A decision passes sub-silentio, in the technical sense that has come to be attached to that phrase, when the particular point of law involved in the decision is not perceived by the court or present to its mind."
(Salmond on Jurisprudence, 12th Edn., p. 153).

In Lancaster Motor Company (London) Ltd. v. Bremith Ltd. the Court did not feel bound by earlier decision as it was rendered 'without any argument,
without reference to the crucial words of the rule and without any citation of the authority'.

entities.text: Lancaster Motor Company (London) Ltd. v. Bremith Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was approved by this Court in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v.
Gurnam Kaur.

entities.text:
Municipal Corporation of Delhi v.
Gurnam Kaur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Bench held that, 'precedents sub-silentio and without argument are of no moment'.
The courts thus have taken recourse to this principle for relieving from injustice perpetrated by unjust precedents.

A decision which is not express and is not founded on reasons nor it proceeds on consideration of issue cannot be deemed to be a law declared to have a binding effect as is contemplated by Article 141.
Uniformity and consistency are core of judicial discipline.
But that which escapes in the judgment without any occasion is not ratio decidendi.

In B. Shama Rao v. Union Territory of Pondicherry it was observed, 'it is trite to say that a decision is binding not because of its conclusions but in regard to its ratio and the principles, laid down therein'.

entities.text: B. Shama Rao v. Union Territory of Pondicherry
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Any declaration or conclusion arrived without application of mind or preceded without any reason cannot be deemed to be declaration of law or authority of a general nature binding as a precedent.
Restraint in dissenting or overruling is for sake of stability and uniformity but rigidity beyond reasonable limits is inimical to the growth of law"

Justice RM Sahai in his concurring opinion in State of UP v. Synthetics and Chemicals Ltd held,
"English courts have developed this principle in relaxation of the rule of stare decisis.

sentences.text: Relevant paras 113,114 and 115 8.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. The grounds taken in the petition of para No. 19 of the rejoinder that the provisions referred in the said para were not brought to the notice of the Hon'ble Supreme Court while rendering the judgment, therefore, the judgment cannot be treated as precedent and cannot be taken.

This Court while going through the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, where it is specifically stated that the Act was under consideration by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, therefore, in such a situation, I cannot say that while the judgment is passed, the Hon'ble Supreme Court was not having the knowledge of the provisions as referred above.
10.The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the said judgment had referred to the provisions contained in the J&K Land Acquisition Act.

The judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which has been relied upon shows that the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, the provisions of J&K Land Acquisition Act, and J&K General Clauses Act as well as Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Removal of Difficulties) Order,
2019, was very much taken into consideration while dealing with the writ petition.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text:
Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Removal of Difficulties) Order,
2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Once the Acts have been referred, it cannot be said that the Hon'ble Supreme Court had no knowledge of the provisions, though, the Act was before then for consideration while rendering the judgment in question, therefore, this argument of learned counsel for the petitioner that these provisions were not brought to the knowledge cannot be accepted, therefore, submission rejected.
11.The judgment rendered in para 5(1) to 7 would also make it clear that provisions of the Act were considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court while rendering the judgment in question.

The judgment,
therefore, cannot be said to be per curiam.
Hence, while relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, no case is made out by the petitioner to interfere, therefore, dismissed.

(VINOD CHATTERJI KOUL) JUDGE Jammu 30.05.2024 Vishal Pritam Singh And Others vs Ut Of J&K And Others on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17998961/
